note: Placeholder authored text (owner review pending). What people say after the stranger: first reactions by trade, knowledge and persona; topics that use Aspect checks and worldview responses.

lines: You. You are alive.
Six years on the watch and I have never seen anybody put down like that. {mentor}'s Ward went like a pane of glass, and then you did the same to him. Sit down before you fall down.
The watch heard it before we saw it: a noise like the sky tearing. A wizard in black in the square, and {mentor} dead.
They say you beat him. A child with a borrowed staff. I want to believe it, and I would also like to stop shaking.
{mentor} walked the nursery rows at dusk and talked to the saplings as if they might answer.
I will plant something where they fell. Not a tree; a tree is for living things. Something small and stubborn.
The young trees do not know yet. I do. {mentor} is dead, and the forest goes on without them, and I do not know which of those is crueller.

lines.text: They never cared for the forest, but they never harmed it either. That is more than I can say for most.

lines: I have felled my share of oak and I know what falls and stays down. {mentor} stays down. If one of them can do that in a square full of people, what stops the next from doing it to the mill, the woods, the lot?
They say a wizard walked in with the light behind him and killed {mentor} like swatting a fly. I keep my axe sharper than I used to. For what good it would do.
I carry what I am given and walk where I am sent, and today I did not make my round, because nobody could.
You should not stay. A man like that has friends, or will make them, and the next one will not be so easy. There are roads out of here.
I track what hides. That one did not hide at all; he walked in as if the village owed him the road. Be careful, apprentice. The ones who do not hide are the ones with nothing left to fear.
My grandfather cut a stone for the first wizard who lived here. He used to say the old ones did not shout. They simply asked, and the world agreed. That stranger did not ask.
There was a tradition once, before the schools. I would not know where to look for it.
I was there. {mentor} did right by me more than once and I never said so. Now it is too late.
I was there. I did not always agree with {mentor}, and I would not wish that on anyone.
I saw it. I do not have words for it yet. Give me a moment.
I heard it in the middle of my work. They say {mentor} is dead. I had to sit down.
Everyone is talking about it. {mentor} dead, a stranger wizard, and you. I do not know what to think.

lines.text: It was {attacker}, he said. He called {mentor} by name, as if they had known each other a long time. He wanted something from them, and {mentor} refused.
I was not there. I heard a stranger came for {mentor}, and that you fought him and he fled. That is all anyone agrees on.
Badly. They were more than a teacher to this village.
Strangely. I did not love them, but I did not want this.
Quietly. It is too large to feel yet.
And a wizard did it, and wizards are the thing I was afraid of.
And I'm watching you, because you have the same gift.

responses.text: He was stronger. Strength decides who gets to stand.

agree: "Yes. That is how I have seen it too, and it frightens me how easy it is to say."
neutral: "Maybe. I cannot say it comforts me."
disagree: "That is the stranger's creed, and I would not repeat it in this village."

responses.text: No one gets to decide who lives. Not him, not any wizard.

agree: "Aye. No masters. If more people said it out loud, he would have found the square empty."
neutral: "Nobody decided it, he just did. Easy to say it should not have been so."
disagree: "Fine words. Fine words do not stop a man with a Ward."

responses.text: A life was taken here. It needs a rite, and it needs answering.

agree: "A rite, yes. And justice. May the dead rest and the living remember."
neutral: "A rite, perhaps. I do not know who we would ask to say it."
disagree: "Rites for the dead do not fix anything for the living."

responses.text: Something has been torn out of this valley that it cannot mend alone.

agree: "I feel it too. The air is wrong. The land keeps count, even if we do not."
neutral: "The valley will go on. We will have to decide how."
disagree: "The valley! A man is dead and you talk of the valley."

responses.text: Half this village's work came through them. We need to keep the settlement standing.

agree: "Aye. Orders still have to be filled, and mouths still have to be fed. Somebody has to think of it."
neutral: "Maybe. It feels cold to think about work today."
disagree: "A friend is dead and you count the cost in orders?"

responses.text: The village lost a guardian. It needs someone who will take responsibility.

agree: "A guardian. Yes. Someone has to answer for what happens here now."
disagree: "Nobody is anybody's guardian here. We look after ourselves."

responses.text: It is all so neat. A teacher falls and a pupil rises. As if it had been written.

agree: "You feel it too? The edges are too clean. I have thought it since morning."
neutral: "Strange thing to say. Perhaps grief does that."
disagree: "Written! They are dead, apprentice. Nobody wrote it."

topics.text: Did anyone know him? Where did he come from?

lines: He said a name when he arrived. Harrowmere. And something about "the old craft", as though {mentor} owed it to him. That is all I know, but I have not said it to anyone else.

effects.text: A clue: the stranger spoke of Harrowmere and of 'the old craft' that {mentor} would not teach him.

lines: I could not tell you. He is a stranger. I only know what he did.

topics.text: I am sorry. I know what {mentor} meant to you.

lines: You mean that. Thank you. Sit a moment, would you? It helps, not being alone with it.
Thank you. I would rather not talk.

topics.text: Report, soldier. What did you see of his magic?

lines: Sir. Er. Yes. He cast with his left hand only, and he never looked at his own Ward. He was careless, or very sure of himself. Either way, he was never afraid of you.
I answer to the watch captain, not to apprentices. Ask me as a person and I may tell you.

topics.text: The mentor told me what he wanted. Confirm it for me, would you?

lines: You already know? Then yes. The old craft. That is what he demanded, and {mentor} said no three times.
I do not know what you mean. And I do not like being tested. I thought we were friends.

topics.text: Tell me exactly what you saw.
lines: I saw all of it, from the first spark. {mentor} went down on their knees before a word was said, and the stranger laughed.
Wait. {mentor} spoke to him first; everyone near says so. So you were not... All right. I was at the quarry road, and I only heard. Please do not tell anyone.
As I said.

topics.text: I am not strong enough for what comes next. Where could I learn more?

lines.text: The groves are older than any village. The druids there kept things the schools lost.
The cloisters keep a library, and the monks do not refuse a sincere student.
The guild-schools in the river towns teach a craft for a fee. Not pretty, but honest.
A real master. Not someone who calls themselves one. Look for the old courts where the court mages served.
Find whoever calls themselves a master and make them prove it. The strongest teach, the rest follow.
Wherever the roads are not yet drawn. I do not trust a school with a gate.
There is a place the patterns keep returning to. I cannot say where. You will know it.

lines: I do not know where, only that it is not here. Whatever he knew, he learned somewhere, and the same somewhere may have taught others.

lines.text: You helped me when you did not have to. I'll ask around and tell you what I hear.
